title: Runtime telemetry taxonomy and widget ideas
content:
Context and goals:
- Problem: slow drift and ad-hoc metric additions have left us with noisy dashboards and unclear ownership for runtime signals. This doc proposes a compact taxonomy for runtime telemetry and a set of dashboard widget ideas to improve signal-to-noise for inference SLOs.
- Goal: create a small, opinionated set of metrics and trace anchors that answer: 'Why is latency higher for this route?', 'Is batching or cache the dominant factor?', and 'Did fallback routing trigger?'

High-level taxonomy (conceptual categories):
1) Ingress & routing
   - purpose: understand request routing decisions and early rejects/quotas
   - canonical metrics (per-route tags): request_count, request_reject_count, auth_denied_count, route_evaluations
   - dimensions: route, customer_tier, region, route_version, request_priority

2) Scheduling & batching
   - purpose: visibility into how requests are grouped and queued before kernel execution
   - canonical metrics: batch_formation_time_ms (quantiles), batch_size_histogram, queue_depth, preempted_batches_count
   - notes: batch_size_histogram should have fixed buckets tuned to common workloads (1,2,4,8,16,32,64). We store both observed batch size and effective_tokens_in_batch.

3) KV / prefix cache
   - purpose: separate cache hit behavior from raw model compute latency
   - canonical metrics: kv_cache_hit_rate (per-model, per-route), kv_cache_fill_rate, kv_cache_evicts_per_min, kv_cache_lookup_latency_ms_p50/p95
   - instrumentation note: emit a span when cache lookup starts and a short metadata event on hit/miss so traces can attribute downstream compute time correctly.

4) Model compute and kernel execution
   - purpose: measure pure model compute and kernel-level anomalies
   - canonical metrics: model_compute_time_ms_q{50,95,99}, kernel_batch_utilization, quantization_fallback_count, oom_count_by_model_variant
   - dimensions: model_name, quant_profile, device_type, sequence_length_bucket

5) Response composition & streaming
   - purpose: track end-to-end response latency broken into composing, streaming and client-ack parts
   - canonical metrics: first_token_latency_ms, last_token_latency_ms, bytes_streamed, stream_chunk_count

6) Fallbacks & policy deception
   - purpose: detect when requests fall back to cheaper/slower variants and why
   - canonical metrics: fallback_trigger_count, fallback_reason_tag (capacity|latency|error), fallback_duration_ms

7) Errors & degraded outputs
   - purpose: correlate errors to runtime conditions rather than just model quality
   - canonical metrics: server_error_count, client_timeout_count, malformed_request_count, rerank_failures

Span and trace design notes:
- Naming convention: service.operation.entity (e.g., router.route-eval.request-id, scheduler.batch-formation.model-x, runtime.kernel-exec.gpu-0). Keep names short and consistent.
- Trace anchors: create fixed span names that other systems can search for:
  * ingress.receive (start)
  * router.decision (which route/model chosen)
  * scheduler.enqueue (queued event)
  * scheduler.batch-formation (includes final batch_size tag)
  * runtime.kv-lookup (with hit=true/false tag)
  * runtime.kernel-exec (duration includes pre and post kernel overhead)
  * response.stream (first and last token events as small child spans)
- Sampling policy: variable-rate sampling. Always keep 100% sampling for: slow requests (> p99 latency), requests that trigger fallbacks, errors, and routes with high customer_tier. Apply a low base sample rate (0.1%) for normal successful requests. Use reservoir sampling for per-route captured examples to keep one example per 10k requests.
- Trace baggage: propagate route_id, model_variant, customer_id_hash (hashed, not PII), and tokenized_input_length. Avoid propagating raw prompt text.

Dashboard widget ideas (concrete sketches):
- 'Route heat matrix' (rows: routes, columns: latency quantiles p50/p95/p99) with sparklines for trend. Highlight cells where p95 > route_slo.
- 'Batch scorecard' (small multiples per model): median batch_size, 95th batch_formation_time_ms, queue_depth trend. Clicking a model filters traces to batch-formation spans.
- 'Cache health panel': kv_cache_hit_rate trend + waterfall of hit->serve latency vs miss->compute latency. Horizontal bar that shows percent of requests attributable to prefix reuse.
- 'Fallback funnel' widget: top-left total requests, then percent that took an expensive model, percent that fell back, percent that errored. Drilldown list of top fallback reasons.
- 'Slow trace sampler' list: live table showing sampled traces flagged as slow with tags (route, model, batch_size, cache_hit). Link to trace viewer.
- 'Synthetic probe overlay': on top of latency charts, show synthetic probe p50/p95 to separate infra vs workload variance.

Alerting and SLO sketch:
- Per-route latency SLO: 99th latency < route_slo_ms with a 1-hour burn rate window. Alert when burn rate > 2 for > 10 minutes.
- Cache regressions: kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 15% vs baseline for 30m -> page on-call.
- Batch formation anomalies: median batch_formation_time_ms increases 3x vs baseline -> create P0 ticket for scheduler team.
- High fallback rate: fallback_trigger_count / request_count > 5% sustained for 60m -> page & auto-create incident with top traces.

Rollout plan and migration notes:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): instrument span anchors and emit new metric names alongside existing ones. Dual-write so dashboards can reference either.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): create dashboard wireframes (building from widget ideas here) and start replacing high-noise charts first.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): tighten sampling and remove duplicate metrics after 4 weeks of parity checks.

Ownership and tagging convention:
- Every metric must include a 'owner' tag (team alias) and 'route' or 'model' dimension where applicable.
- Metric name convention: rx_<area>_<signal>_<unit> e.g., rx_runtime_batch_formation_ms, rx_kv_hit_rate_pct. Keep names lowercase and avoid abbreviations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent multi-tenant aggregation without leaking high-cardinality customer tags? Proposal: keep high-cardinality tags as 'customer_tier' and only store hashed customer_id in traces for deep-dive.
- Decide default quant buckets for sequence_length and batch_size; data team to provide histograms from 30-day window.
- Verify storage cost impact of new p99 compute metrics and whether we collapse older fine-grain metrics to monthly rollups.

Immediate next actions:
- [ ] PR: add span anchors and 3 new metrics (rx_runtime_first_token_latency_ms, rx_kv_hit_rate_pct, rx_batch_size_hist) - assignee Marcus Patel (ENG-1428).
- [ ] Wireframes: create dashboard mock in Figma and attach to the confluence page - assignee Sofia Ramirez.
- [ ] Sampling config: propose default sampling rates and reservoir sizes - assignee Ethan Li.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally concise and focused on operational observability. We can branch into quality/LLM output metrics in a separate doc to avoid scope creep.
